s.g: An expression of relief, relaxation, comfort, confusion, understanding, wonder, awe, etc. according to uttered inflection.
ex: Ah, I understand now.
Ah! It's good to be back home!

s.g: A syllable used to fill space, particularly in music.
Used condescendingly, somewhat like “see?” or “I told you so”.
ex: Pitch contour: mid-falling /ɑ(ː)˧˨/, falling /ɑ(ː)˦˨/, sometimes nasalized

s.g: Yuck.
An instance of the interjection ah.
ex: the crowd's oohs and ahs at the fireworks

s.g: To give a cry of "ah".
Marks a yes–no tag question prompting the listener to clarify or confirm something.
ex: Pitch contour: low-mid /ɑ(ː)˨/, [ä˨]
You’re dyslexic ah?

s.g: Reinforces a short, non-rhetorical wh-question.
ex: Pitch contour: rising /ɑ(ː)˨˦/
How do you delete this row ah?

s.g: Emphasizes the need for absolute confirmation, permission or acknowledgment.
ex: Pitch contour: rising /ɑ(ː)˨˦/
Don’t drink and drive ah...

s.g: A particle indicating the topic of a sentence from its comment.
ex: Pitch contour: rising /ɑ(ː)˨˦/
The drilling upstairs ah, non-stop leh.

s.g: A prefix of Chinese origin used with a shortened form of given names to express familiarity, roughly equivalent to a nickname.
ex: Ah Ming moved out of Chinatown last year.

s.g: prefix for attack helicopter, helicopter gunship designations

of: most often indicating that the speaker is using a Scottish or American

s.g: An exclamation of understanding, realization, invention, or recognition.
ex: Aha! That will work.

s.g: An exclamation of surprise, exaltation, or contempt.
ex: Aha! Now I've got you!

s.g: At or towards the front; in the direction one is facing or moving.
ex: The island was directly ahead.
Just ahead you can see the cliffs.

s.g: So as to be further advanced, either spatially or in an abstract sense; to be superior.
ex: He finished two laps ahead of me.
In all of his classes Jack was ahead.

s.g: In or for the future.
ex: There may be tough times ahead.
You've got to think ahead so as not to be unprepared.

s.g: To a later time.
ex: Set the clock ahead an hour.
Push the deadline ahead a day, from the 20th to the 21st.

s.g: The sound of a quiet cough or of clearing one's throat.
Demanding attention.
ex: Ahem! Could we please get started?

s.g: Expresses disapproval or annoyance.
ex: Ahem! In case you didn't notice, I did my share of the work, too.

s.g: Indicates subtle sarcasm, polite lying, or euphemism.
ex: I really (ahem!) liked the chocolate broccoli surprise.
